Even young children can tell the difference between an asthma attack (primarily difficulty exhaling) and a VCD attack (primarily difficulty inhaling).

Knowing the difference between the two will help those who have both know when to use the rescue inhaler prescribed or when to use the breathing recovery exercises trained by a speech-language pathologist.
The exact cause of VCD is not known, and it is unlikely that a single underlying cause exists.
Several contributing factors have been identified, which vary widely among VCD patients with different medical histories.
